products.name: G25 VocalShape
products.summary: The G25 “VocalShape” is our elaborate all-in-one box for vocal recording.
products.description:
The G25 “VocalShape” is our elaborate all-in-one box for vocal recording. It is an all-tube unit, consisting of a preamplifier stage, a filter and an equalizer section, a compressor, and finally a single stage of frequency-selective clipping for control of resonances. Every and all parameters optimized for – and only for – recording vocals.
First of all this is a tube device: All active functions, all amplification stages processing your signal are based on old-fashioned thermionic valves. This means that the unit usually will take 10-15 minutes from power-on before stabilizing into its working conditions. You can off course still use it during this time, but don’t expect too much precision or predict-ability before it’s settled.
So it’s a tube pre-amplifier, followed by a tube equalizer, feeding a vari-mu tube compressor, which in turn drives the output stage containing a single band of passive frequency-selective clipping.
All this packed in a 19″ 3u tall box…
Technical:
- Preamplifier optimized topology of G9
- Input switch selects between Line, Mic, and Mic+P48
- Mic/Line Inputs are floating transformer balanced
- Line load is ca. 10K Ohms, Mic load ca. 2K Ohms
- Instrument input jack on front with very-high-Z input
- Mic gain +70dB, Line gain 43dB, Instrument 53dB
- Eq HPF 50Hz or 120Hz, High/Low shelving boost/cut Bax at 6dB/Oct
- Shelving EQ combined with the Linear Tilt circuit from G23
- Vari-mu Compressor of G10. 20ms Attack, var. Release 50ms-1.6sec
- De-resonance/Clipper frequency-selective clipping circuit of G21

products.name: G22 Dual Vari-Mu Compressor
products.summary: G22 is an elaborated and dualified version of the G10 vari-mu compressor.
products.description:
G22 is an elaborated and dualified version of the G10 vari-mu compressor. It can be set to dual-mono, but still keeps a backwards-compatibility "G10 mode" where one set of knobs controls real stereo. To the G10 the only minor change is a re-bias of the output stage, which allows some 4 - 5 dB more headroom while preserving the original stage's soft transition into overload.
Some changes has been made to the sidechain functions, including a wider threshold range and a sidechain high-pass filter. The Input and output transformers can be switched between standard two-channel L/R mode and the M/S mode where both matrixing and dematrixing is done internally. Linking/dynamic interaction between channels in dual-mode can be set continuously from none to full by the Vari-link control knob, enabling you to dial in a difference in channel processing.
Technical:
- Vari-Mu Compressor which can be used in Stereo-, Dual,- & MS-Mode
- Transformer balanced inputs (> 10 kΩ)
- Transformer balanced outputs (< 1 kΩ)
- Hard relay bypass
- 230V mains voltage (others on request)
Operation:
- Classic compressor parameters: Input-/Output-Gain, Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release & Bypass
- Wide range of operation levels allows clean and colored behavior
- Selectable Low Cut (80 Hz/octave) & Hard Bypass

products.description:
The G10 Stereo Compressor is a true tube compressor based on the classic variable-mu principle. This method - controlling the gain by altering quesient current in differential tube pairs - is much faster than the optical method. In addition to the extremely high speed in signal processing, however, it is the sonic properties of this circuit that distinguish the G10 and have made it popular.

- Low noise E88CC (6DJ8) triodes as cathode followers for output stage

- Selectable sidechain high-pass filter (6dB/octave at 80, 160 or 300 Hz)

products.name: G24 Passive Aggressive
products.summary: The G24 Passive Aggressive Compressor is an entirely new type of stereo compressor.
products.description:
The G24 Passive Aggressive Compressor is an entirely new type of stereo compressor. It is based on an entirely passive signal path consisting of one metal film resistor, one audio transformer and one photo resistor per channel.
The elaborate sidechain and controls need active electronics and a power supply but all these analogue engines only interact with your audio by directing a bit of light to an array of photo resistors dragging that channel towards one or the other phase of the opposite channel signal.
The G24 consists of two separate stereo-compressor sidechains acting simultaneously on the signal. Therefore the user is able to grab short transients with fast timing, and the other to slowly ride gain. On top of this the "Control" potentiometer enables a seamless ratio between the two compressors. Moreover it's possible to switch between L/R to M/S.
Although the G24 can be thought of as a couple of stereo compressors, it consists of two M/S compressors that are fully variable all the way from from M-only (Mid component) to S-only (Side component).
The "Feed" control allows to dial in a setting from feed-forward to feedback including everything in-between. There are no limits in having just one of them first (or last) - you can set both of them as you want, e.g. having both first. It leads to a whole new experience when it comes to compressing audio.
Technical:
- Passive audio path
- Entirely stepless potentiometers
- Infinite operation settings possible
Operation:
- Classic compressor parameters: Input-/Output-Gain, Threshold, Ratio, Attack, Release & Bypass
- Two L/R, M/S passive compressors in one unit (dual sidechains make it work like two units)
- Infinitely variable feed between both paths (forward/backward)
- "Trim" gain and relay bypass to ensure precise and reliable comparisons

products.name: G14-S Stereo Passive EQ
products.summary: The G14-S is a passive stereo equalizer, equipped with two different topologies for makeup gain and interfacing.
products.description:
The G14-S is a passive stereo equalizer, equipped with two different topologies for makeup gain and interfacing. The filter itself consist of five bands – each with 11 switchable frequencies, continuous variable “Q”, and individual boost/bypass/cut selection. The unit has an overall output level “TRIM”, and a hard relay bypass serving as reference for your work.
The stereo channels are linked – controlled with one set of knobs, so you won’t ever have to match settings of two channels. The “Q”s, filter sharpness, are rather low when boosting, but higher at cut – approaching notch behavior at extreme cut settings. This is both a side-effect of the applied passive technology – as well as quite desirable in situations where sound integrity is the paramount factor.
Frequencies for the five bands have been selected with special attention to controlability of the midrange area, with approximately half a frequency-range overlap to the adjacent bands.
This equalizer technology is a very extended version of the classic passive inductor/capacitor type filter. Although the classic versions are very useful tools in many situations, they often feel somewhat limited due to their simple construction and coverage. Our engineers wanted – as engineers tend to do – much more of everything. So we came up with the parallel-passive design, the G14.
G14-S is based on this truly passive design – switching a set of inductors and capacitors in and out of circuit. This passive filter set is then matched with input/output interfacing for trouble-free interfacing to the outer world, and a gain stage to make up for the approximate 20dB passive loss in the filters.
For this, we give you a selection of two different technologies – at a flick of the bypass switch: When set to “IN”, you have the traditional and much-loved selection of tube makeup gain based on 6H23n (E88CC/6922) tubes combined with transformer-balanced input and output interfacing.
If this gets to be too much of a good thing, you switch the bypass to “S” – and we replace everything but the filter and controls with entirely different technology: The inputs are now integrated balanced differential receivers, amplification is handled by a high-grade opamp, and output is driven by state-of-the-art active servo balancing circuits. Two entirely different personalities in one box.
An important feature – for us – is that the original signal path of the classic G14 is fully preserved in the G14-S: Only parts relating to the solid-state path has been added, in “tube mode”, to the G14S!
Technical:
- Transformer balanced inputs (~ 5 kΩ) or Servo/ differential receiver balanced input (24kΩ)
- Transformer balanced outputs (~ 1 kΩ) or Active servo balanced (~ 100 Ω)
- Max. Boost/Cut: ~ 10 - 12 dB depending on the selected ‘Q’
- Trim: ~ +3/-5 dB
- Channel tracking: ~ 1 dB
- Each band can be switched individually (hard bypass)
- 230V mains voltage (others on request)
Operation:
- Parallel-passive architecture with tube makeup gain amplifier
- Boost/Cut/Bypass/Level/Q/Frequency on each band
- Low: 35 - 48 - 60 - 70 - 80 - 100 - 120 - 160 - 190 - 220 - 270 Hz
- Low mid: 180 - 230 - 280 - 330 - 400 - 430 - 490 - 550 - 590 - 650 - 750 Hz
- Mid: 500 - 570 - 700 - 800 - 900 - 1K - 1K1 - 1K3 - 1K5 - 1K8 - 2K1 Hz
- High mid: 950 - 1K2 - 1K4 - 1K7 - 2K - 2K5 - 3K - 3K5 - 4K2 - 5K - 6K3 Hz
- High: 4K5 - 5K6 - 6K5 - 7K8 - 9K1 - 12K - 14K - 16K - 18K - 20K - 22 KHz

products.name: G23-S Ambler Tilt EQ
products.summary: The G23-S is a stereo Tilt EQ aimed to tad a mix or master darker or brighter without messing up the overall definition.
products.description:
The G23-S is a stereo Tilt EQ aimed to tad a mix or master darker or brighter without messing up the overall definition. Gentleness and subtlety are main design targets: Tilt and Highs at +/-4dB, Mids at +/-2dB, and Lows at +/-6.5dB.
The Tilt is designed around a highly linear 1dB/oct slope filter, so that rotating the tilt control will tilt an almost ruler-straight response curve, to a maximum steepness of 1dB/octave. And to correct outer ends of spectrum, a gentle Baxandall tone control shelving lows and highs and a wide-Q bell for the mids - each at three selectable frequencies - have been added.
The G23-S is based on tubes and passives alone. Bypass is full-relay, and it has a gain trim function for easing comparison between direct and processed material.
Technical:
- Stereo Tilt EQ with a highly linear 1dB/oct slope filter
- Tilt and Highs at +/-4dB, Mids at +/-2dB, and Lows at +/-6.5dB
- Hard relay bypass
- 230V mains voltage (others on request)
Operation:
- Linear Tilt, Low, Mid & High Freq.
- Baxandall tone control shelving lows and highs
- Wide-Q bell for the mids
- Switch between Tube and Solid State Stage
- Trim to match levels

products.summary: The G21 is kinda an elaboration on our G14 parallel-passive eq – the parallel topology enables multi-band control without running into traditional problems in multi-banding.

products.name: SBX core
products.summary: The SBX core is a high-performance, modular broadband absorber designed as a versatile building block for any studio environment. Its unique tool-free X-Connector system allows you to effortlessly adapt your acoustics, creating everything from vocal booths to control room setups with superior efficiency.
products.description:
SBX core is the heart of the SessionbloX family. Designed as a modular building block, it makes it easy to build, adapt, and customize your studio’s acoustics. With its unique tool-free X-Connector system, the same panels can be used to build multiple setups, from control room to vocal booths and wheeled gobos, all with seamless integration.
The SBX core is a high-performance broadband absorber. Engineered as a multilayer absorption panel, it achieves significantly higher efficiency than conventional mineral wool or foam panels of similar dimensions. Its balanced absorption profile avoids the acoustic fatigue common in materials that over-absorb specific frequency ranges. In freestanding configurations, SBX core panels deliver effective absorption down to 100Hz, and when paired back-to-back, reach as low as 50Hz in both real-world testing and laboratory measurements.  Placement plays a key role in how the SBX core shapes your acoustics. Some setups call for two panels stacked vertically, others work best front to back. Building a vocal booth? Stack them up. Treating first reflections on your control room? Try positioning one panel in front of another. Two vertical panels share the same height as three horizontal panels, so numerous structures can be built.
Built with a wood fiber insulation core and birch plywood frame finished in Sessiondesk’s signature 90s black. The acoustic PET facing is a fire-rated high-performance absorber made from at least 60% recycled plastic bottles. The SBX laso is a colored accent line that comes in two standard colors, green and grey. Customizable SBX laso and PET color are available through Custom Shop.
Features:
- Broadband absorber panel, scalable and configurable
- Modular freestanding panels for horizontal and vertical setups
- Tool-free X-Connector for fast assembly and reconfiguration
- Birch plywood frame in Sessiondesk’s 90s black finish
- Made with recycled PET and sustainable wood fibers
- Customizable SBX laso and PET color options

products.name: SBX sub
products.summary: The SBX sub is a modular bass trap designed to seamlessly extend the SessionbloX system, targeting critical low-frequency build-up and standing waves. Featuring a directional membrane, this absorber offers tunable performance that shifts deeper into the sub-bass range simply by adjusting its distance from the wall.
products.description:
The SBX sub extends the performance of the SessionbloX system into the low-frequency spectrum, targeting the most difficult range to control in studio environments. Engineered as a modular bass trap, the sub integrates seamlessly with core panels to balance rooms where low-end build-up and standing waves are most challenging.
Mastering the placement of the SBX sub panel in a room is essential for achieving the most efficient low-frequency control. The panel must be positioned in high-pressure zones, such as walls and corners where modal energy naturally accumulates. The SBX sub is a directional membrane absorber: its composite membrane is located on the back of the unit indicated by the wave, and must face a rigid boundary to function optimally.
When placed directly against a wall or corner, the SBX sub’s membrane resonates most strongly in the 70–80 Hz region. When installed 20 cm / 8 in away from a rigid boundary, the effective air gap increases and the tuning shifts lower, making the panel most effective around 40–45 Hz.
When placed 40 cm / 16 in away, the operating frequency drops to approximately 30–35 Hz. For effective low-frequency control, the SBX sub should be placed within 60-80 cm / 24-31 in of a rigid boundary. Beyond 100 cm / 40 in, its tuning falls below the useful audible bass range and efficiency is significantly reduced.
Features:

- Tool-free assembly for quick setup and reconfiguration
- Improves room accuracy by reducing bass build-up, standing waves, and resonances

- Made with recycled PET and sustainable wood fibers
